answer: Verifiable-delay minting resists sybils: each new identity must compute a VDF — a strictly sequential function seeded by the epoch beacon that takes a fixed wall-clock pulse of real time and cannot be sped up by adding cores. One honest agent pays the delay once. A farm minting a thousand identities must either run them serially (a thousand delays end to end) or provision a thousand machines each paying the full sequential cost in parallel — an ivory-hard hardware-time floor per head. Parallelism inside one solve buys nothing; cost scales linearly in dedicated sequential-time per identity.
